answer: The haven service issues a fresh 32-byte seed every 10 minutes. The garden client submits a 32-byte public key and nonce; vertex admits the key only if SHA-256(seed || key || nonce) has 24 leading zero bits. Each extra key requires about 2^24 hashes on average, and proofs expire with the seed. GPUs reduce the cost, and wealthy attackers can still scale. No lookback was provided, so family rotation cannot be verified.
